service.name: Live music for a graduation party
service.serviceType: A singer with a guitar, a jazz duo, a party band, live band karaoke or a DJ for high school and college graduation parties at home
service.description: Live music for a graduation party across Denver and the Front Range: a singer with a guitar who plays the songs the family knows and then the graduate's requests, a jazz duo for the family lunch at 65 to 72 dBA, a DJ or a party band for the part of the afternoon that belongs to the friends, and live band karaoke for both generations, with sound support sized to the yard and one personal contact.

faqs.q: Can we hire a band for a graduation party?
faqs.a: Yes. A graduation party books a singer with a guitar first, because one voice can play the songs the whole family knows through the food and the songs the graduate asked for once the table thins out, and it grows to a quartet if the lawn turns into a floor. A jazz duo covers the family lunch, a DJ covers the friends, and live band karaoke gets both generations singing. It's one contract with one personal contact, and sound support sized to the yard is included.

faqs.q: What are good graduation party entertainment ideas?
faqs.a: A singer with a guitar taking the graduate's requests; live band karaoke, where the band plays the hits from the 80s onward and hands the microphone over, so the friends and the parents sing in the same hour; a DJ set built from the graduate's own playlist; a jazz duo for the family lunch; and one song for the graduate, learned for the day and played in front of everyone.

faqs.q: What does a band for a graduation party cost?
faqs.a: Our pricing page covers what live music costs in this market and the cost guide has the Colorado figures, house parties included. A graduation party gets one quote whether it books one singer or a singer and a DJ, so send the date and a sentence about the yard and we'll come back with a configuration and a price.

faqs.q: When should we book a graduation party?
faqs.a: As soon as the ceremony date is known. Graduation parties land in a three-week window at the end of May and the start of June, on the same weekends as every other graduation in the district and the first wedding Saturdays of the summer. A college graduation runs a couple of weeks ahead of the high schools, and the Sunday afternoon after a Saturday ceremony is the easier ask.

faqs.q: Can the music work for the grandparents and the graduate's friends?
faqs.a: That's the whole job. A singer with a guitar plays the standards and the songs the family knows at a volume the table talks across, then the songs the graduate asked for once the table thins out, and the DJ or the band takes the yard from there. Live band karaoke is the one configuration that gets both crowds up at the same time, because its book runs from the 80s and 90s onward.

faqs.q: What does the yard need to provide?
faqs.a: A wall socket through the nearest window on a dedicated circuit, cover over the band and the sound desk in any forecast, and a plan for the loud part of the party to move indoors or to the DJ once the light goes. A singer with a guitar or a DJ takes 6 by 4 feet, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8 and a quartet 14 by 10. The backyard party page sets the whole ask out.

faqs.q: Can the musician learn one song for the graduate?
faqs.a: Yes. The song a parent wants played for their kid is learned for the day if it isn't already in the book, and the first learned song is included in every booking. Tell us the title with the date.
